claim: The surgical history reports, in the case of Corporal A. W. McCausland, that a shell struck the outer side of the left thigh, inflicting a terrible flesh wound eight inches long by four in width, with ragged edges.

source.edition: Part III, Volume II, Surgical History, first issue, Washington: Government Printing Office, 1883 (chapters X to XV: lower extremities, miscellaneous injuries, complications, anaesthetics, the medical staff and materia chirurgica, transportation of the wounded)
